approved: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Amendment (Compliance Measures No. 2) Bill 2013

Backed the bill implementing recommendations of the 2010 Montara inquiry into offshore petroleum safety, described a new floating LNG plant about 490 metres long, and said the oil and gas industry, responsible for 30 cents of every private-sector dollar invested in Australia, is investing around $200 billion over five years, warning budget changes to thin capitalisation and exploration rules threaten that investment.

Supported the bill, recalling that the National Offshore Petroleum Safety and Environmental Management Authority was created in response to the 2009 Timor Sea oil spill, noted the upstream oil and gas sector generated around $35.6 billion in 2008-09 employing over 10,000 people, and said emissions in the national electricity market have fallen by about 10 million tonnes since the carbon price began.

Backed the bill and reaffirmed the coalition's implacable opposition to oil and gas exploration in the Great Barrier Reef, and contrasted this cooperative bill with the government's carbon tax revenue forecasts of $12.10 a tonne in 2015-16 and $18 in 2016-17, which he said are double and triple likely market prices, creating budget black holes of $2 billion and $4 billion in those years.

Summed up the bill as strengthening offshore petroleum regulation following the August 2009 Montara wellhead release and the deaths of two workers, aged 32 and 60, on the Stena Clyde rig in the Otway Basin in August 2012, introducing new enforcement tools including adverse publicity orders and a polluter-pays duty.
